groups.title: Reviewer access and the iPhone build

items.text: Sign in with the demo account in App Review Information. Check it will not expire, and your contact details are current.
items.why: A reviewer who cannot sign in, or cannot reach you with a question, cannot finish testing the app.

items.text: Check your hosting, database and AI credits will not pause or run out while Apple reviews the app.
items.why: If the server is asleep or out of credit when the reviewer opens the app, it looks broken or unfinished.

items.text: Install your TestFlight build on an iPhone, and an iPad if you can. Try every login button and every main screen.
items.why: A crash, a login that fails or a broken layout that exists only in the iPhone build is invisible to FixThenShip's web test.

items.text: Check your review notes give steps to each main feature, say where purchases are, and explain what the reviewer cannot try.
items.why: Apple says generic descriptions will be rejected, and a feature the reviewer cannot find may be treated as missing.

items.text: Check the iPhone build does something your website in Safari cannot, and name it in the review notes.
items.why: Apple can reject an app it sees as only a repackaged website, and FixThenShip cannot judge that for you.

items.text: Open the Privacy Policy URL in App Store Connect. It must load and say what you collect and who receives it.
items.why: Apple requires this link in App Store Connect as well as in the app. The policy must say what data you collect and how you use it, and cover outside services that receive it. Apple also asks you to say clearly when data goes to a third-party AI (5.1.2(i)).

items.text: Read your App Privacy answers in App Store Connect. They must cover everything the app, its analytics and ad tools collect.
items.why: Apple treats these answers as part of the listing, so leaving out data the app really collects counts as inaccurate information.

items.text: On the iPhone build, trigger each permission request: camera, location, tracking if you use ad tools. Each must say plainly why.
items.why: Apple asks that each permission text clearly explains how the data is used (5.1.1(ii)), and requires permission through App Tracking Transparency before tracking (5.1.2(i)).

items.text: Look at your screenshots. Most must show the app in use as it looks today, not a splash or login screen.
items.why: Screenshots that show only a splash or login page, or an old design, do not meet Apple's rule that they show the app in use.

items.text: Check your iPad screenshots were taken on an iPad or the iPad simulator, not resized or stretched from iPhone ones.
items.why: App Store Connect asks for screenshots for each device size, and a founder was rejected for iPad screenshots resized from iPhone ones. Guideline 2.3.3 asks that screenshots show the app in use.

items.text: Read your description and screenshot captions. Remove any feature the app does not have yet, and say which ones cost extra.
items.why: A listing that promises features the app lacks, or hides that a feature costs extra, counts as inaccurate.

items.text: Check the app name and subtitle contain no other brands' names such as 'GPT', no prices and no lists of keywords.
items.why: Apple's rule bans packing the name or keywords with trademarks, popular app names or prices, so such a listing can be rejected.

items.text: Search your listing text and screenshots for 'Android', 'Google Play', other stores' logos or an Android status bar. Remove them.
items.why: Apple does not allow the names, icons or pictures of other mobile platforms or app stores in a listing.

groups.title: Purchases and subscriptions (skip if the app sells nothing)

items.text: In App Store Connect, check the Paid Apps Agreement is active and every in-app purchase is added to this submission.
items.why: Without an active agreement you cannot submit purchases, and purchases the reviewer cannot find or use count as an incomplete app.

items.text: If you sell subscriptions, check your App Store listing links to your Terms of Use as well as your Privacy Policy.
items.why: Apple's subscriptions page says both the app and its App Store listing must carry these links.

items.text: On the TestFlight build, tap Restore Purchases and check a purchase made with a test account comes back.
items.why: A real restore only happens in the iPhone build, so FixThenShip cannot test it, and a broken one is a known rejection reason.

groups.title: Support, age rating and legal basics (reminders, not legal advice)

items.text: Open the Support URL in App Store Connect. It must load and show a current way to contact you.
items.why: Apple requires a support link with up-to-date contact details for every app, and FixThenShip cannot see the one in your listing.

items.text: Check your age rating answers in App Store Connect. They should match the app, including chat, user posts or mature themes.
items.why: Apple asks for honest answers, and a rating that does not match what is in the app can lead to rejection.

items.text: Keep proof that you own or may use every brand name, image, font and icon in the app and listing.
items.why: Apple does not allow other people's trademarks or copyrighted work without permission, and FixThenShip cannot tell who owns what.

items.text: In App Store Connect, check your build shows no 'Missing Compliance' warning. If it does, answer the encryption questions.
items.why: Apple asks about encryption when you submit a version, and a build marked 'Missing Compliance' needs your answer before it can move on.
